claims.text: Tobacco smoking was responsible for an estimated 467,000 deaths in US adults in 2005.
High blood pressure was responsible for an estimated 395,000 deaths in US adults in 2005.
Overweight-obesity was responsible for an estimated 216,000 deaths in the US in 2005.
Physical inactivity was responsible for an estimated 191,000 deaths in the US in 2005.
High dietary salt was responsible for an estimated 102,000 deaths in the US in 2005.
Low dietary omega-3 fatty acids were responsible for an estimated 84,000 deaths in the US in 2005.
High dietary trans fatty acids were responsible for an estimated 82,000 deaths in the US in 2005.
Current alcohol use averted an estimated 26,000 deaths from ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and diabetes in the US in 2005.

Current alcohol use caused an estimated 90,000 deaths from non-protective cardiovascular diseases, cancers, liver cirrhosis, pancreatitis, alcohol use disorders, injuries, and violence in the US in 2005.

evidence.description: In 2005, tobacco smoking was responsible for an estimated 467,000 (95% CI 436,000-500,000) deaths, accounting for about one in five or six deaths in US adults.
High blood pressure was responsible for an estimated 395,000 (95% CI 372,000-414,000) deaths, accounting for about one in five or six deaths in US adults.
Overweight-obesity (216,000; 188,000-237,000) was responsible for nearly 1 in 10 deaths.
Physical inactivity (191,000; 164,000-222,000) was responsible for nearly 1 in 10 deaths.
High dietary salt (102,000; 97,000-107,000) was among the dietary risks with the largest mortality effects.
Low dietary omega-3 fatty acids (84,000; 72,000-96,000) was among the dietary risks with the largest mortality effects.
High dietary trans fatty acids (82,000; 63,000-97,000) was among the dietary risks with the largest mortality effects.
26,000 (95% CI 23,000-40,000) deaths from ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and diabetes were averted by current alcohol use.

Averted deaths from alcohol use were outweighed by 90,000 (95% CI 88,000-94,000) deaths from other cardiovascular diseases, cancers, liver cirrhosis, pancreatitis, alcohol use disorders, road traffic and other injuries, and violence.

methodologies.name: Comparative risk assessment modeling
methodologies.description: Estimated disease-specific deaths attributable to non-optimal exposure levels of 12 dietary, lifestyle, and metabolic risk factors using national exposure surveys and mortality statistics combined with relative risk estimates from epidemiological meta-analyses.
datasets: National Center for Health Statistics mortality statistics
conditions: Etiological risk estimates adjusted for major potential confounders and regression dilution bias
